role.zh: 与特奥蒂瓦坎有关的军事首领

summary.en: Siyaj K'ahk' ("Fire Is Born") arrived at Tikal in January 378, the day its king died, and installed a new dynasty linked to Teotihuacan. Inscriptions name him as overlord of several Petén cities; he is last mentioned around 402.
summary.zh: 西亚赫·卡克（意为“火焰诞生”）于378年1月抵达蒂卡尔，当天该城国王死去，他扶植了一个与特奥蒂瓦坎有关的新王朝。铭文称他为佩滕多座城市的宗主，最后一次被提及约在402年。

label.en: Arrives at Tikal; king Chak Tok Ich'aak I dies
label.zh: 抵达蒂卡尔，国王查克·托克·伊查克一世死去
在瓦哈克通被记为征服者

label.en: Installs Yax Nuun Ahiin I as king of Tikal
label.zh: 立亚什·努恩·阿因一世为蒂卡尔国王

sources.title: Simon Martin & Nikolai Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens (2nd ed., 2008)
David Stuart, "The Arrival of Strangers: Teotihuacan and Tollan in Classic Maya History" (2000)
Wikipedia: Siyaj K'ak'

name.en: K'inich Janaab Pakal I (Pakal the Great)
name.zh: 基尼奇·哈纳布·巴加尔一世（巴加尔大帝）

role.zh: 帕伦克国王

summary.en: Pakal became king of Palenque at 12 in 615 and reigned for 68 years, rebuilding his war-battered kingdom into a centre of art and architecture. He built much of the Palace and was buried in the Temple of the Inscriptions, where his tomb was found in 1952.
summary.zh: 巴加尔于615年12岁时成为帕伦克国王，在位68年，把饱受战火摧残的王国重建为艺术和建筑中心。他修建了王宫的大部分建筑，死后葬于铭文神庙，其陵墓于1952年被发现。

label.zh: 帕伦克遭卡拉克穆尔洗劫

label.en: Dedicates House E of the Palace
Dies; buried in the Temple of the Inscriptions

sources.title: Simon Martin & Nikolai Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens (2nd ed., 2008)
UNESCO World Heritage: Pre-Hispanic City and National Park of Palenque
Britannica: Pacal
Wikipedia: K'inich Janaab' Pakal

story.en:
Pakal inherited a kingdom in crisis. Calakmul's armies had sacked Palenque in 599 and again in 611, and the royal line passed through his mother, Lady Sak K'uk', who probably ruled as regent when he took the throne on 29 July 615, aged twelve. The inscriptions describe the time before as one when the gods were "lost".

Pakal's answer was building. Over seven decades he raised the Palace with its unique four-storey tower, its galleries of stucco and its sculpted captives in the East Court, the trophies of wars against Calakmul's allies such as Santa Elena. Texts in the Temple of the Inscriptions trace his ancestry back to a mythical first mother, making his mother's claim to the throne divine.

When he died on 28 August 683, aged 80, he had outlived most of his children. His son K'inich Kan Bahlam II finished his pyramid and the Cross Group. Pakal's skeleton suggested to some a younger man, raising a debate about whether the inscriptions' ages could be true, but recent studies of bone and teeth support an elderly king.
story.zh:
巴加尔继承的是一个危机中的王国。卡拉克穆尔的军队曾于599年和611年两度洗劫帕伦克，王统经由他的母亲萨克·库克夫人传承；615年7月29日他12岁登基时，母亲很可能摄政。铭文把此前的时代描述为众神“迷失”的时代。

巴加尔的回应是营建。七十年间，他建起王宫，包括其独一无二的四层塔楼、灰泥装饰的长廊，以及东院中雕刻的俘虏像，那是与卡拉克穆尔盟邦（如圣埃伦娜）作战的战利品。铭文神庙中的文字把他的世系追溯到一位神话中的始祖母，从而使其母亲的王位继承权具有神性。

683年8月28日他以80岁高龄去世时，已经送走了大多数子女。他的儿子基尼奇·坎·巴拉姆二世完成了他的金字塔和十字神庙群。巴加尔的骨骼曾让一些人以为属于较年轻的人，从而引发铭文所记年龄是否属实的争论，但近年对骨骼和牙齿的研究支持他是一位高龄国王。

name.zh: 尤克努姆·钦二世（尤克努姆大帝）

role.en: King of the Kaanul (Snake) kingdom at Calakmul
role.zh: 卡拉克穆尔卡努尔（蛇）王国国王

summary.en: Ruling from 636 to 686, Yuknoom Ch'een II made the Kaanul dynasty, by then based at Calakmul, the most powerful in the Maya lowlands, installing or supervising kings at Cancuén, Dos Pilas, Naranjo, Piedras Negras and elsewhere in a network that encircled Tikal.
summary.zh: 尤克努姆·钦二世于636至686年在位，使此时以卡拉克穆尔为都的卡努尔王朝成为玛雅低地最强大的王朝。他在坎昆、多斯皮拉斯、纳兰霍、彼德拉斯内格拉斯等地册立或监督国王，形成包围蒂卡尔的网络。

label.en: Born into the Kaanul royal family (Dzibanche origins)
label.zh: 生于卡努尔王族（起源于济班切）

label.en: Takes B'alaj Chan K'awiil of Dos Pilas as vassal
label.zh: 收多斯皮拉斯的巴拉赫·陈·卡维尔为附庸

label.en: Defeats Tikal and drives out its king
label.zh: 击败蒂卡尔并驱逐其国王

label.en: Dies at Calakmul after 50 years' rule
label.zh: 统治50年后卒于卡拉克穆尔

sources.title: Simon Martin & Nikolai Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens (2nd ed., 2008)

Wikipedia: Yuknoom Ch'een II

name.zh: 六天夫人（瓦克·查尼尔·阿豪）

role.zh: 纳兰霍王后、摄政

summary.en: A princess of Dos Pilas, daughter of B'alaj Chan K'awiil, Lady Six Sky arrived at Naranjo in 682 to refound its ruined dynasty. She ruled as regent for her young son K'ak' Tiliw Chan Chaak, led wars in which captives were taken in her name, and was shown on stelae trampling bound prisoners.
summary.zh: 六天夫人是多斯皮拉斯国王巴拉赫·陈·卡维尔之女，682年来到纳兰霍重建已遭毁灭的王统。她为年幼的儿子卡克·蒂利夫·陈·查克摄政，领导了以她的名义俘获敌人的战争，石碑上的她脚踏被缚的俘虏。

label.en: Arrives at Naranjo to restore its dynasty
Her son K'ak' Tiliw Chan Chaak crowned at five
label.zh: 其子卡克·蒂利夫·陈·查克五岁登基

sources.title: Simon Martin & Nikolai Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens (2nd ed., 2008)
Kathryn Reese-Taylor et al., "Warrior Queens among the Classic Maya", in Ancient Maya Women (2002)
Wikipedia: Lady Six Sky

name.zh: 瓦沙克拉胡恩·乌巴·卡维尔（“十八兔”）

role.zh: 科潘第13位国王

summary.en: Copán's 13th king (r. 695–738) filled the Great Plaza with a forest of high-relief stelae, rebuilt the ballcourt and called Copán one of the four great kingdoms of the Maya world. He was captured and beheaded by his vassal K'ak' Tiliw Chan Yopaat of Quiriguá in 738.
summary.zh: 科潘第13位国王（695—738年在位）在大广场上竖起林立的高浮雕石碑，重建球场，并称科潘为玛雅世界四大王国之一。738年，他被附庸基里瓜国王卡克·蒂利夫·陈·约帕特俘获并斩首。

label.zh: 开始在大广场竖立石碑

label.en: Installs K'ak' Tiliw Chan Yopaat at Quiriguá
label.zh: 立卡克·蒂利夫·陈·约帕特为基里瓜统治者
在基里瓜被俘并遭斩首

sources.title: Simon Martin & Nikolai Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens (2nd ed., 2008)
UNESCO World Heritage: Maya Site of Copan
Wikipedia: Uaxaclajuun Ub'aah K'awiil

role.en: Mixtec warlord and king of Tututepec and Tilantongo
role.zh: 米斯特克军事领袖、图图特佩克与蒂兰通戈国王

summary.en: The best-documented ruler of the Mixtec codices, Eight Deer rose from a secondary lineage of Tilantongo to found the coastal kingdom of Tututepec and unite much of the Mixteca through conquest and alliances, including with a Toltec-style lord named Four Jaguar. He was captured and sacrificed in 1115.
summary.zh: 八鹿是米斯特克手抄本中记载最详尽的统治者。他出身蒂兰通戈的旁支，建立沿海王国图图特佩克，并通过征服和结盟（包括与一位名为“四美洲豹”的托尔特克式君主结盟）统一了米斯特克地区大部。1115年他被俘并被献祭。

label.en: Takes power at Tututepec on the coast
label.zh: 在沿海的图图特佩克掌权

label.en: Nose pierced as a lord; rules Tilantongo
label.zh: 行穿鼻礼成为贵族，统治蒂兰通戈

label.en: Conquers the Hill of the Wasp and kills rivals
label.zh: 征服“黄蜂山”并杀死对手

sources.title: Codex Zouche-Nuttall (British Museum Am1902,0308.1)
Alfonso Caso, Interpretación del Códice Colombino (1966)
Wikipedia: Eight Deer Jaguar Claw

note: Dates derive from Caso's correlation of the Mixtec calendar; places of conquests are approximate.

story.en:
Eight Deer's life is told in pictures. The Mixtec screenfold books, painted on deer hide and read in zigzag, show him as a youth making offerings in caves, consulting the aged priestess Lady Nine Grass at the oracle of Chalcatongo, and leading warriors by canoe and on foot.

According to the codices, he was a son of the high priest of Tilantongo by a second wife, so he had no clear right to rule. He made his base on the Pacific coast at Tututepec, then allied with a powerful lord, Four Jaguar, who wears Toltec-style dress and is sometimes connected with Tula or Cholula. In a famous scene Four Jaguar pierces Eight Deer's nose for a turquoise nose-ornament, the mark of supreme rank.

Eight Deer then conquered dozens of towns and married several noblewomen, among them Lady Thirteen Serpent, a granddaughter of his half-brother's killer. He also had rival heirs killed. In the end, the codices say, he was captured and sacrificed at 52 by a young lord, Four Wind, son of one of his victims, who later married Eight Deer's daughter and founded new dynasties.
story.zh:
八鹿的一生是用图画讲述的。米斯特克折页手抄本绘在鹿皮上，以“之”字形顺序阅读，描绘他少年时在洞穴中献祭、在查尔卡通戈神谕所请教年迈的女祭司“九草夫人”，以及率领武士乘独木舟和步行出征的情景。

据手抄本记载，他是蒂兰通戈大祭司与第二位妻子所生的儿子，因此并无明确的继位权。他以太平洋沿岸的图图特佩克为根据地，随后与一位强大的君主“四美洲豹”结盟；此人身着托尔特克式服饰，有时被与图拉或乔卢拉联系起来。在一个著名场景中，四美洲豹为八鹿穿鼻，佩上绿松石鼻饰，这是至高身份的标志。

此后八鹿征服了数十座城镇，迎娶了多位贵族女子，其中包括杀害其同父异母兄长之人的孙女“十三蛇夫人”。他还下令杀死了与他争位的继承人。手抄本说，他最终在52岁时被年轻的贵族“四风”俘获并献祭；四风是他所害之人的儿子，后来娶了八鹿的女儿，开创了新的王朝。

role.en: Tlatoani of Texcoco, poet and engineer
role.zh: 特斯科科君主、诗人、工程师

summary.en: Prince of Texcoco who saw his father killed by the Tepanecs and spent years in exile, Nezahualcoyotl helped found the Triple Alliance in 1428 and ruled Texcoco from 1431. He was famed as a lawgiver, builder of the dike that divided Lake Texcoco and of gardens at Texcotzingo, and as a poet.
summary.zh: 内萨瓦尔科约特尔是特斯科科王子，曾目睹父亲被特帕内克人杀害，流亡多年。他于1428年参与建立三国同盟，自1431年起统治特斯科科。他以立法者、修建分隔特斯科科湖的大堤和特斯科辛戈园林的建造者，以及诗人的身份而闻名。

label.en: Watches Tepanec soldiers kill his father Ixtlilxochitl
label.zh: 目睹特帕内克士兵杀死其父伊斯特利尔索奇特尔
流亡特拉斯卡拉和韦霍钦戈
参与摧毁阿斯卡波察尔科

label.en: Directs construction of the great dike across Lake Texcoco
label.zh: 主持修建横跨特斯科科湖的大堤

Miguel León-Portilla, Fifteen Poets of the Aztec World (1992)

role.zh: 特诺奇蒂特兰大君主

summary.en: Ruler of Tenochtitlan from 1502, Moctezuma Xocoyotzin centralised the empire and extended it to its greatest size. He received Hernán Cortés in November 1519, was taken hostage, and died in June 1520 in disputed circumstances during the Spanish siege of his palace.
summary.zh: 蒙特祖马·索科约钦自1502年起统治特诺奇蒂特兰，加强中央集权，使帝国疆域达到极盛。1519年11月他接见埃尔南·科尔特斯，随即被扣为人质，1520年6月西班牙人在其宫殿被围期间死去，死因至今存疑。

label.en: New Fire ceremony on Huixachtlan (Cerro de la Estrella)
label.zh: 在韦伊沙赫特兰（星辰山）主持新火仪式

label.en: Meets Cortés on the causeway (8 November)
label.zh: 在堤道上会见科尔特斯（11月8日）

label.en: Dies a captive in the Palace of Axayacatl
label.zh: 在阿哈雅卡特尔宫中作为囚徒死去

role.zh: 特诺奇蒂特兰末代大君主

summary.en: A cousin of Moctezuma, Cuauhtémoc ("Descending Eagle") was chosen ruler after Cuitláhuac died of smallpox and led the defence of Tenochtitlan in 1521. Captured on 13 August, tortured for gold, he was hanged by Cortés in 1525 during the expedition to Honduras. He is honoured as a national hero of Mexico.
summary.zh: 夸乌特莫克（意为“降落之鹰”）是蒙特祖马的堂弟，在奎特拉瓦克死于天花后被推举为君主，于1521年领导特诺奇蒂特兰保卫战。8月13日被俘后遭酷刑逼问黄金，1525年在远征洪都拉斯途中被科尔特斯绞死。他被尊为墨西哥的民族英雄。

name.zh: 马林钦（马林切，堂娜·玛丽娜）

role.zh: 翻译、中间人

summary.en: A Nahua noblewoman sold as a girl to Maya traders, Malintzin was one of 20 women given to Cortés at Potonchán in 1519. Speaking Nahuatl and Maya, and soon Spanish, she became his indispensable interpreter and adviser in the conquest of Mexico and bore his son Martín.
summary.zh: 马林钦是纳瓦族贵族女子，幼年被卖给玛雅商人。1519年在波通昌，她是被送给科尔特斯的二十名女子之一。她通晓纳瓦特尔语和玛雅语，很快又学会西班牙语，成为科尔特斯征服墨西哥时不可或缺的翻译和顾问，并为他生下儿子马丁。

label.zh: 生于夸察夸尔科斯附近

label.en: Given to the Spaniards at Potonchán
label.zh: 在波通昌被送给西班牙人
在科尔特斯与蒙特祖马之间翻译

label.en: Gives birth to Martín Cortés at Coyoacán
label.zh: 在科约阿坎生下马丁·科尔特斯
在奥里萨巴附近嫁给胡安·哈拉米略

sources.title: Camilla Townsend, Malintzin's Choices: An Indian Woman in the Conquest of Mexico (2006)
Bernal Díaz del Castillo, Historia verdadera de la conquista de la Nueva España (written c. 1568)
Wikipedia: La Malinche

note: Her birth (c. 1500) and death (c. 1529) years are estimates.

story.en:
Everything we know about Malintzin comes from others: Spanish soldiers who called her Doña Marina, and Nahua painters who drew her standing beside Cortés, larger than he, speaking. Bernal Díaz says she was the daughter of a lord near Coatzacoalcos who was given away as a child after her father died, ending up as a slave among the Chontal Maya of Tabasco.

When the Spaniards landed at Potonchán in March 1519 and defeated its warriors, she was among twenty women handed over as tribute. Cortés soon discovered that she spoke Nahuatl as well as Maya, so with the shipwrecked Spaniard Jerónimo de Aguilar translating Maya into Spanish, he could talk to the Aztecs. Within months she spoke Spanish herself. To Indigenous peoples Cortés himself became known as "Malinche", the master of Malintzin.

She was at every turning point: at Cholula, where Spanish sources say she uncovered a plot; at the meeting with Moctezuma; on the Noche Triste. After the conquest she bore Cortés a son, Martín, and was married off to the conquistador Juan Jaramillo. In the 19th century nationalist writers made her a traitor, and malinchismo came to mean preferring foreign things. Historians such as Camilla Townsend see instead a young enslaved woman who survived by making difficult choices.
story.zh:
我们对马林钦的了解全部来自他人：称她为“堂娜·玛丽娜”的西班牙士兵，以及把她画在科尔特斯身旁（比他还高大）、正在说话的纳瓦画师。贝尔纳尔·迪亚斯说，她是夸察夸尔科斯附近一位领主的女儿，父亲死后幼年被送走，最终沦为塔巴斯科琼塔尔玛雅人的奴隶。

1519年3月西班牙人在波通昌登陆并击败当地武士时，她是被作为贡品交出的二十名女子之一。科尔特斯很快发现她既会玛雅语又会纳瓦特尔语，于是由落难西班牙人赫罗尼莫·德阿吉拉尔把玛雅语译成西班牙语，他便能与阿兹特克人交谈了。几个月内，她自己也学会了西班牙语。在原住民口中，科尔特斯本人被称为“马林切”，即马林钦的主人。

每一个转折关头都有她的身影：在乔卢拉，西班牙史料说她揭穿了一个阴谋；在会见蒙特祖马时；在悲痛之夜。征服之后，她为科尔特斯生下儿子马丁，随后被嫁给征服者胡安·哈拉米略。19世纪的民族主义作家把她塑造成叛徒，“马林切主义”一词也成了崇洋媚外的代名词。而卡米拉·汤森等史学家看到的，是一位靠艰难抉择求得生存的年轻女奴。

role.zh: 征服者

summary.en: A minor Extremaduran noble who settled in Hispaniola and Cuba, Cortés led the expedition of 1519 that, with Indigenous allies, overthrew the Aztec Empire in 1521. He governed New Spain until 1524, explored the Pacific coast and Baja California, and died in Spain still litigating over his privileges.
summary.zh: 科尔特斯出身埃斯特雷马杜拉小贵族，先后在伊斯帕尼奥拉岛和古巴定居。1519年他率远征队出发，在原住民盟友的帮助下于1521年推翻阿兹特克帝国。他统治新西班牙至1524年，勘察太平洋沿岸和下加利福尼亚，最终在西班牙去世，至死仍在为自己的特权打官司。

label.zh: 在下加利福尼亚的拉巴斯登陆

summary.en: Cortés's second-in-command, notorious for the Toxcatl massacre of 1520, Alvarado conquered the highland Maya of Guatemala and El Salvador from 1524 and governed Guatemala until his death, when his horse fell on him during the Mixtón War.

name.zh: 巴托洛梅·德拉斯·卡萨斯

role.en: Dominican friar, historian and defender of Indigenous rights
role.zh: 多明我会修士、史学家、原住民权利捍卫者

summary.en: A former encomendero who renounced his Indigenous labourers in 1514, Las Casas spent fifty years denouncing Spanish atrocities in the Americas. He influenced the New Laws of 1542, served as Bishop of Chiapas and debated Juan Ginés de Sepúlveda at Valladolid in 1550–1551; his Brief Account of 1552 was read across Europe.
summary.zh: 拉斯卡萨斯原是委托监护主，1514年放弃了归他役使的原住民。此后五十年，他不断揭露西班牙人在美洲的暴行。他影响了1542年的《新法》，出任恰帕斯主教，并于1550至1551年在巴利亚多利德与胡安·希内斯·德塞普尔韦达辩论；他1552年的《西印度毁灭述略》传遍欧洲。

label.en: Renounces his encomienda at Sancti Spíritus, Cuba
label.zh: 在古巴圣斯皮里图斯放弃委托监护权

label.en: Bishop of Chiapas at Ciudad Real
label.zh: 在雷阿尔城任恰帕斯主教
在巴利亚多利德与塞普尔韦达辩论

sources.title: Lawrence A. Clayton, Bartolomé de las Casas: A Biography (2012)
Britannica: Bartolomé de Las Casas
Wikipedia: Bartolomé de las Casas

story.en:
Las Casas first came to Hispaniola as a settler in 1502, at about eighteen, and received Taíno labourers in encomienda. He took part as a chaplain in the conquest of Cuba, where he witnessed the massacre of Caonao in 1513: Spanish soldiers, he wrote, suddenly drew their swords and killed men, women and children sitting peacefully in a village square.

In 1514, preparing a Pentecost sermon at Sancti Spíritus, he read a verse of Ecclesiasticus, "The bread of the needy is their life; he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood", and decided he could no longer hold Indigenous people. He gave up his encomienda and began a lifelong campaign at the Spanish court. An early proposal that Africans rather than Indians be used as labourers became a regret he later recorded with shame.

He tried a peaceful colony in Venezuela, which failed, and a peaceful conversion of the Verapaz in Guatemala. As bishop of Chiapas he refused absolution to Spaniards who held Indigenous slaves, provoking such fury that he left after two years. In the great debate at Valladolid he argued that the peoples of America were fully rational and that war against them was unjust. His Brief Account, translated and illustrated with gruesome engravings by Protestant printers, fed the "Black Legend" of Spanish cruelty.
story.zh:
拉斯卡萨斯约18岁时于1502年以移民身份来到伊斯帕尼奥拉岛，分得一批泰诺人作为委托监护劳工。他作为随军神父参与征服古巴，并在1513年目睹了卡奥瑙大屠杀：他写道，西班牙士兵突然拔剑，砍杀了安静地坐在村庄广场上的男女老少。

1514年，他在圣斯皮里图斯准备圣灵降临节布道时，读到《德训篇》中的一句话：“穷人的饼是他们的命，夺去它的人就是流人血的人。”他决定不能再役使原住民。他放弃了委托监护权，开始了在西班牙宫廷长达一生的奔走。他早年曾提议用非洲人代替印第安人充当劳力，后来他羞愧地记下了对此的悔恨。

他在委内瑞拉尝试建立和平殖民地，结果失败；又在危地马拉的韦拉帕斯尝试和平传教。担任恰帕斯主教时，他拒绝为蓄养原住民奴隶的西班牙人赦罪，激起众怒，两年后便离开了。在巴利亚多利德的大辩论中，他主张美洲各民族完全具有理性，对他们发动战争是不义的。他的《述略》被新教印刷商翻译出版，配上骇人的版画，助长了关于西班牙人残暴的“黑色传说”。

summary.en: A Spanish settler who escaped his debts on Hispaniola by stowing away to Darién in 1510, Balboa became leader of the colony of Santa María la Antigua and in 1513 led the first European expedition to reach the Pacific from the Americas. He spent his last years as a hermit beside the chapel. His historical existence is debated; he was canonised in 2002 as the first Indigenous saint of the Americas.

Recalled to Spain, he wrote the Relación de las cosas de Yucatán, the main colonial source on Maya life, whose "alphabet" later helped decipher the script. He returned as bishop in 1573.

name.en: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
name.zh: 胡安娜·伊内斯·德拉克鲁斯修女

role.zh: 诗人、剧作家、学者

summary.en: A self-taught prodigy who dazzled the viceregal court, Juana Inés de Asbaje became a Hieronymite nun in 1669 so she could study. Her convent cell held one of the largest libraries in New Spain; her poetry, plays and her defence of women's learning make her the greatest writer of colonial Spanish America.
summary.zh: 胡安娜·伊内斯·德阿斯巴赫是自学成才的神童，曾令总督宫廷倾倒。为了能够读书治学，她于1669年成为圣哲罗姆会修女。她的修道小室藏有新西班牙最大的图书室之一；她的诗歌、戏剧以及为女性求学的辩护，使她成为殖民时期西属美洲最伟大的作家。

label.zh: 生于圣米格尔-内潘特拉

label.en: Learns to read at Panoayan, near Amecameca
label.zh: 在阿梅卡梅卡附近的帕诺阿扬学会读书

label.en: Lady-in-waiting to the vicereine at court
label.zh: 在宫廷担任总督夫人的侍女

label.en: Takes vows at the convent of San Jerónimo
label.zh: 在圣哲罗姆修道院发愿

label.en: Writes the Reply to Sor Filotea
label.zh: 写下《致菲洛特亚修女的答复》

label.en: Dies nursing sisters in an epidemic
label.zh: 在照料染疫修女时去世

sources.title: Octavio Paz, Sor Juana, or, The Traps of Faith (1988)
Britannica: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
Wikipedia: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz

note: Her birth year is 1648 or 1651: a baptismal record suggests 1648, while her first biographer, Diego Calleja, gave 1651.

story.en:
Juana learned to read at three, following her sister to school, and as a girl begged her mother to let her dress as a boy to attend the university in Mexico City. Instead she devoured her grandfather's library. At about sixteen she joined the household of the vicereine, the Marquise of Mancera, and the viceroy arranged for some forty professors to examine her in theology, philosophy, mathematics and poetry. She answered, he said, "like a royal galleon fending off a few canoes".

With no wish to marry, she chose the convent as the only place where a woman could live among books. In the Hieronymite convent of San Jerónimo she wrote love poems, comedies, religious dramas, carols and the long philosophical poem Primero sueño, and gathered scientific instruments. Her best-known satire turns on men who blame women for the very faults that men themselves provoke.

In 1690 the Bishop of Puebla published her critique of a famous sermon and added a letter, signed "Sor Filotea", telling her to turn to religious subjects. Her Reply, a defence of women's right to learn, was her last major work. Under pressure from the Church, she sold her library around 1693, signed a renewal of her vows in blood, and died two years later nursing her sisters during an epidemic.
story.zh:
胡安娜三岁时跟着姐姐上学便学会了读书；少女时，她恳求母亲让她女扮男装去墨西哥城上大学。母亲没有答应，她便如饥似渴地读完了外祖父的藏书。约十六岁时，她进入总督夫人曼塞拉侯爵夫人的府中，总督安排约四十位教授考问她神学、哲学、数学和诗歌。总督说，她应答起来“犹如一艘皇家大帆船击退几只独木舟”。

她无意婚嫁，选择修道院作为一个女子能与书为伴的唯一场所。在圣哲罗姆修道院，她写下情诗、喜剧、宗教剧、颂歌和长篇哲理诗《初梦》，还收集科学仪器。她最著名的讽刺诗嘲讽男人指责女人，而那些过错恰恰是男人自己引起的。

1690年，普埃布拉主教出版了她对一篇著名布道词的评论，并附上一封署名“菲洛特亚修女”的信，要她转向宗教题材。她的《答复》为女性求学的权利辩护，成为她最后一部重要作品。在教会的压力下，她约于1693年卖掉了藏书，用自己的血签署重申誓愿的文书，两年后在一场瘟疫中照料修女时去世。

role.en: Privateer and lieutenant governor of Jamaica
role.zh: 私掠船长、牙买加副总督

summary.en: A Welshman who came to Jamaica around the time of its conquest, Morgan led buccaneer raids on Spanish America under commissions from Jamaica's governor: Puerto Príncipe (1668), Portobelo (1668), Maracaibo (1669) and Panama (1671). Knighted, he served three terms as acting governor of Jamaica and died at Port Royal.
summary.zh: 摩根是威尔士人，大约在英国征服牙买加时来到该岛。他持牙买加总督颁发的委任状，率领海盗袭击西属美洲：太子港（今卡马圭，1668年）、波托韦洛（1668年）、马拉开波（1669年）和巴拿马（1671年）。他受封爵士，三度代理牙买加总督，最终卒于罗亚尔港。

summary.en: An Akan woman probably born in what is now Ghana, Nanny led the Windward Maroons in the Blue Mountains during the First Maroon War, from a stronghold known as Nanny Town. In 1740 she received a land grant that became Moore Town. Jamaica named her a National Hero in 1976.
summary.zh: 南妮是阿坎族女性，可能生于今加纳。第一次马龙战争期间，她以“南妮镇”为据点，在蓝山领导迎风区马龙人。1740年她获得一块赐地，后来发展为摩尔镇。1976年牙买加将她列为民族英雄。

label.zh: 生于黄金海岸（阿坎人地区）

label.zh: 在南妮镇领导迎风区马龙人

sources.title: Karla Gottlieb, The Mother of Us All: A History of Queen Nanny, Leader of the Windward Jamaican Maroons (2000)
Mavis C. Campbell, The Maroons of Jamaica 1655–1796 (1988)
Wikipedia: Nanny of the Maroons

note: Her life is known from oral tradition and a few British records; dates are approximate.

story.en:
British documents mention her only a handful of times: a soldier's boast of having killed "Nanny, the rebels' old obeah woman", and a 1740 patent granting "Nanny and the people now residing with her" 500 acres in the parish of Portland. Everything else comes from Maroon oral tradition, which remembers her as a spiritual leader and military strategist who never surrendered.

Nanny Town sat high in the Blue Mountains above the Stony River, reachable only by narrow paths that a few defenders could hold. Traditions tell how Nanny organised ambushes in which Maroons disguised with leaves attacked soldiers in single file, how she trained warriors in the abeng horn signals used to pass messages across the valleys, and how she caught British bullets and threw them back, a story that reflects the Maroons' belief in her spiritual power.

British troops captured Nanny Town in 1734, but the Windward Maroons regrouped. After Cudjoe's Leeward Maroons made peace in 1739, the Windward Maroons under Quao signed their own treaty. Nanny's image appears on Jamaica's 500-dollar note.
story.zh:
英国文献只零星几次提到她：一名士兵吹嘘杀死了“南妮，叛匪的老巫婆”；1740年的一份特许状把波特兰区的500英亩土地授予“南妮及现与她同住的人们”。其余的一切都来自马龙人的口述传统，他们记得她是一位从未投降的精神领袖和军事谋略家。

南妮镇高踞蓝山之中、斯托尼河上方，只有几条窄路可以通达，少数守卫者便能扼守。传说讲述南妮如何组织伏击，让身披树叶伪装的马龙人袭击单列行进的士兵；如何训练战士使用“阿本”号角信号在山谷间传递消息；以及她如何接住英国人的子弹再扔回去，这个故事反映了马龙人对她灵力的信仰。

英军于1734年攻占南妮镇，但迎风区马龙人重新集结。1739年库乔领导的背风区马龙人议和之后，夸奥领导的迎风区马龙人也签订了自己的条约。南妮的肖像印在牙买加500元纸币上。

summary.en: Born enslaved on the Bréda plantation and freed in the 1770s, Toussaint joined the 1791 uprising, rose to command its armies, allied with France after it abolished slavery, expelled the British and Spanish and ruled Saint-Domingue under his own 1801 constitution. Seized by Napoleon's general Leclerc in 1802, he died in a French fortress.

Sudhir Hazareesingh, Black Spartacus: The Epic Life of Toussaint Louverture (2020)

story.en:
Toussaint Bréda was in his late forties, a freed coachman and small landowner who had once owned a few slaves himself, when the uprising began in 1791. Literate, devout and a skilled healer with herbs, he became a doctor to the rebel camps and then a commander. In 1793 he took the name Louverture, "the opening", announcing: "I want liberty and equality to reign in Saint-Domingue."

He first fought for Spain, which promised freedom to rebel soldiers. When the French Republic abolished slavery in 1794, he switched sides with his disciplined army, drove out the British by 1798 and occupied Spanish Santo Domingo in 1801. To revive the economy he forced former slaves back to plantation labour as paid workers, a policy that cost him popular support. His constitution of 1801 made him governor for life.

Napoleon saw an insubordinate subject. When Leclerc's army landed in 1802, Toussaint fought, then made peace; in June he was invited to a meeting, seized and shipped to France. Boarding the ship he warned that in overthrowing him the French had cut only the trunk of the tree of liberty, which would grow again from its many deep roots. He died of cold and neglect in a cell in the Jura mountains in April 1803.
story.zh:
1791年起义爆发时，杜桑·布雷达已年近五十，是一位获得自由的车夫和小地主，自己也曾拥有过几名奴隶。他识文断字，笃信宗教，精通草药医术，先是在起义营地行医，后来成为指挥官。1793年，他改名卢维杜尔，意为“开口”，宣称：“我要让自由与平等在圣多明各占据统治地位。”

他起初为许诺给起义士兵自由的西班牙作战。1794年法兰西共和国废除奴隶制后，他带着纪律严明的军队改换阵营，到1798年赶走英国人，1801年占领西属圣多明各。为了恢复经济，他强令前奴隶以领取报酬的劳工身份回到种植园劳动，这一政策使他失去了民心。他1801年的宪法规定他为终身总督。

在拿破仑眼中，他是一个不服管束的臣属。1802年勒克莱尔的军队登陆后，杜桑先是抵抗，后来议和；6月他应邀出席一次会面，遭到逮捕并被押上开往法国的船。登船时他警告说，法国人推翻他，只是砍倒了自由之树的树干，它会从许多深扎的根上重新长出来。1803年4月，他在汝拉山区的牢房中因寒冷和疏于照料而死。

summary.en: A Zapotec orphan from the mountains of Oaxaca who learned Spanish at twelve, Juárez became a lawyer, governor of Oaxaca and leader of the Liberal Reform. As president from 1858 he won the Reform War and resisted the French intervention until Maximilian's execution in 1867. He is honoured for the maxim that respect for the rights of others is peace.

story.en:
Juárez was three when his parents died, and he grew up herding sheep in the Zapotec village of Guelatao. At twelve, speaking almost no Spanish, he walked to the city of Oaxaca, where a Franciscan lay brother, Antonio Salanueva, took him in and sent him to the seminary. He chose law instead of the priesthood and rose through Oaxaca's liberal politics to become governor.

Exiled by Santa Anna in 1853, he rolled cigars in New Orleans with other exiles and planned the Revolution of Ayutla. Back in power, the "Ley Juárez" of 1855 abolished the special courts of clergy and army, opening the Reform. When conservatives revolted in 1858, Juárez, as head of the Supreme Court, became constitutional president and governed from Veracruz, where he issued the laws separating Church and state.

During the French intervention he led a government on wheels, travelling by black carriage across the north to Paso del Norte on the US border, never leaving Mexican soil. In 1867, refusing pleas to spare Maximilian, he declared that among individuals as among nations, respect for the rights of others is peace. The border town of Paso del Norte was renamed Ciudad Juárez in his honour.
story.zh:
华雷斯三岁时父母双亡，在萨波特克村庄格拉陶放羊长大。十二岁时，几乎不会说西班牙语的他步行到瓦哈卡城，方济各会世俗修士安东尼奥·萨拉努埃瓦收留了他，送他进入神学院。他没有当神父，而是选择了法律，在瓦哈卡的自由派政坛中步步高升，直至出任州长。

1853年他被圣安纳流放，在新奥尔良与其他流亡者一起卷雪茄，筹划阿尤特拉革命。重新掌权后，1855年的“华雷斯法”废除了教士和军人的特别法庭，开启了改革运动。1858年保守派叛乱时，身为最高法院院长的华雷斯成为宪法总统，在韦拉克鲁斯主政，并在那里颁布了政教分离的法律。

法国干涉期间，他领导着一个“车轮上的政府”，乘黑色马车穿越北方，一直退到美国边境的北方隘口，却始终没有离开墨西哥领土。1867年，他拒绝了宽恕马克西米连的请求，宣称无论个人之间还是国家之间，尊重他人的权利即和平。边境城镇北方隘口后来改名为华雷斯城以纪念他。

story.en:
Anenecuilco had been fighting the neighbouring sugar haciendas over its land for centuries, and in 1909 its elders chose the thirty-year-old Emiliano Zapata to guard the village's colonial land titles. He was not a peon but a small farmer and a renowned horseman who trained horses for rich landowners. When the courts failed, the villagers took back their fields by force.

Zapata joined Madero's revolt in 1911, but when Madero told him to disarm before any land was returned, he broke with him. The Plan of Ayala, drafted with the schoolteacher Otilio Montaño in November 1911, demanded that land, woods and water usurped by haciendas be restored, with "Reform, Freedom, Justice and Law" as its motto. Federal generals burned villages across Morelos, but Zapata's peasant army, fighting by day and farming by night, could not be destroyed.

In 1919 Colonel Jesús Guajardo pretended to defect and invited Zapata to the hacienda of Chinameca; as he rode through the gate, a guard of honour shot him. Many in Morelos refused to believe he was dead, saying he had escaped to the hills on his white horse. Land reform under the 1917 Constitution, and the Zapatistas of 1994, carried his name forward.
story.zh:
几个世纪以来，阿内内奎尔科一直与邻近的蔗糖庄园争夺土地。1909年，村中长老推选三十岁的埃米利亚诺·萨帕塔保管村里殖民时期的地契。他不是雇农，而是小农，也是为富有地主驯马的著名骑手。法庭不能主持公道，村民们便用武力收回了自己的田地。

1911年萨帕塔加入马德罗的起义，但马德罗要他在归还任何土地之前先解除武装，他便与之决裂。1911年11月他与教师奥蒂略·蒙塔尼奥共同起草的《阿亚拉计划》要求归还被庄园侵占的土地、森林和水源，口号是“改革、自由、正义与法律”。联邦将领在莫雷洛斯各地焚烧村庄，但萨帕塔那支白天打仗、夜里种地的农民军始终无法被消灭。

1919年，赫苏斯·瓜哈尔多上校假装倒戈，邀请萨帕塔到奇纳梅卡庄园；萨帕塔骑马进门时，仪仗队向他开枪。莫雷洛斯的许多人不肯相信他已经死去，说他骑着白马逃进了山里。1917年宪法下的土地改革以及1994年的萨帕塔运动延续了他的名字。

summary.zh: 里维拉在墨西哥求学后旅欧十四年，曾以立体主义风格作画，1921年回国后成为墨西哥壁画运动的领军人物，在墨西哥和美国的公共建筑上绘满描绘历史、劳动与工业的史诗场景。

role.zh: 圣萨尔瓦多大主教、圣人

summary.en: A cautious, bookish priest who became archbishop of San Salvador in 1977, Romero was transformed by the murder of his friend Rutilio Grande into the country's foremost voice against repression. He was shot while saying Mass in 1980 and canonised in 2018.
summary.zh: 罗梅罗原是一位谨慎、好学的神父，1977年出任圣萨尔瓦多大主教。挚友鲁蒂利奥·格兰德遇害使他转变为全国反对镇压的首要声音。1980年他在主持弥撒时遭枪杀，2018年被封为圣人。

role.en: K'iche' Maya human rights activist, Nobel Peace laureate
role.zh: 基切玛雅人权活动家、诺贝尔和平奖得主

summary.en: A K'iche' Maya woman from Quiché whose father, mother and brother were killed during the civil war, Menchú went into exile and told her story in the testimonio I, Rigoberta Menchú (1983). She received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992 for her work for Indigenous rights and reconciliation.
summary.zh: 门楚是来自基切省的基切玛雅女性，她的父亲、母亲和兄弟都在内战中遇害。她流亡海外，在口述实录《我，里戈韦塔·门楚》（1983年）中讲述了自己的经历。1992年，她因致力于原住民权利与和解而获得诺贝尔和平奖。
